name: Deed of settlement company (English unincorporated joint-stock company)
period: c.1720-1844 (Bubble Act 1720 to the Joint Stock Companies Act 1844); ALL CODED CELLS REST ON 1790-1827 EVIDENCE
key_source:
SCOPE, WRITTEN 2026-09-05 BECAUSE THE WORKING SLUG NAMED A CLASS AND THE ROW MUST FIX ITS OWN REFERENT: the English UNINCORPORATED JOINT-STOCK COMPANY constituted by DEED OF SETTLEMENT - a partnership whose elaborately drafted articles excluded the default partnership rules and settled legal title to the circulating trade assets on a fixed body of trustees, with control divided between directors, a general court of proprietors and those trustees. CONSTITUTIVE INSTRUMENT: the deed of settlement (the articles of association), a private deed, with no Royal Charter, patent or Act of Parliament. Televantos's own glossary treats 'deed of settlement company' and 'joint stock company' as one term: 'A business which raised capital by issuing shares and/or bonds. This was distinct from a typical partnership, where the partners who managed the business provided the capital. Legally, deed of settlement companies were partnerships, but made use of some rules of trusts law in an attempt to emulate the benefits of incorporation' (printed 183).
THE UNIT IS THE DEED-OF-SETTLEMENT COMPANY AND NOT THE WIDER CLASS OF ENGLISH ASSOCIATIONS CONSTITUTED BY TRUST DEED, AND THE REASON IS EVIDENTIAL RATHER THAN TIDY. Televantos's chapter 2 treats TWO trust-using business forms, and they take OPPOSITE VALUES on the census's owner-shielding question. The deed-of-settlement company had none: its shareholders were partners, personally liable without limit, and clauses purporting to limit that liability 'were not fully effective' (44-46, 172). The TESTAMENTARY TRADING TRUST did: on Ex p Garland (1804) the trustee's indemnity, and so the trade creditors' reach into the testamentary estate, was capped at the sum the will set aside, which Televantos calls in terms 'an example of how trusts could create limited liability trading entities' (56-60). A single row spanning both would take both values on AP3 and LR1, which is the condition under which voc was split on 2026-08-29 and under which partenrederij was held apart from the open rederij on 2026-08-29. The testamentary trading trust is in any case not an association - it has no members - and is proposed as an ACQUISITION, not as a row.
ALSO OUT OF SCOPE: the ordinary Regency partnership of owner-managers (Televantos chapter 1), whose default rules this form's deed exists to displace; jointly run shipping and mining businesses, which 'were not treated as partnerships' (16 n 5); and chartered or statutory corporations, whose privileges 'lay in the gift of the Crown or Parliament' (172).
BOUNDARY WITH THE EXISTING joint_stock ROW, RESOLVED ON THE EVIDENCE AND FLAGGED FOR DOCUMENTATION. joint_stock reads 'Joint-stock corporation | European | 17c onward | Harris 2020' and carries NO SCOPE NOTE, and Televantos's glossary makes 'joint stock company' a synonym for the present form. But joint_stock is NOT uncoded - it carries two cells, and its LP1=1 has the cell note 'chartered legal personhood', which fixes its referent as the CHARTERED corporation. This row codes LP1=0. The two therefore differ on the first characteristic either touches and there is no coding collision. A draft scope note for joint_stock, to be applied with this batch rather than ahead of it, is at proposed-of/PATCH-joint-stock-scope-2026-09-05.md; it also flags that joint_stock is on its face an umbrella over the three coded voc rows.
PERIOD AND EVIDENCE ARE NOT CO-EXTENSIVE, AND THAT IS THIS ROW'S MAIN WEAKNESS - the partenrederij problem again. The period claimed runs from the Bubble Act 1720, which by making it an offence to raise capital by issuing transferable stock without Charter or Act drove counsel to invent the form (35-36), to the Joint Stock Companies Act 1844, which forced large partnerships to incorporate by registration (52). EVERY CODED CELL RESTS ON EVIDENCE FROM 1790-1827, the period Televantos's book covers, supplemented by his reading of DuBois (1938) for the eighteenth century and of Freeman, Pearson and Taylor (2012), who find that 209 of the 224 large partnerships they examine between 1720 and 1840 used trusts in their articles (31). FP4 in particular would flip at 1844 by definition.

name: Antwerp general commercial partnership (societas generalis / compagnie), Costuymen Impressae phase
period: 1582-1608 as enacted law, on evidence reaching back to c.1540; the Impressae remained the operative compilation in Antwerp after 1608, so the phase boundary is TEXTUAL rather than practical

SCOPE, WRITTEN 2026-09-05 BECAUSE THE SOURCE WRITES ABOUT 'las sociedades' GENERALLY AND THE ROW MUST FIX ITS OWN REFERENT: the Antwerp GENERAL COMMERCIAL PARTNERSHIP - societas generalis, compagnie - constituted by a contrato de sociedad and governed by the default rules of Antwerp municipal customary law. IT IS A FORM AND NOT A DOCTRINAL CATEGORY, ON DE RUYSSCHER'S OWN TERMS: the 1554 official declaration names a societas generalis as a thing of which one is a socius (240-241); the constitutive instrument is the contrato de sociedad; the compilations give it chapters of its own (Impressae 1582 cap. 58, with caps. 51-52 on the fund; Compilatae 1608 part 4 cap. 9); and the form has a named pool, the corpo or capitale, with default rules attaching to it. BUT THE ROW INHERITS THE SOURCE'S CENTRAL FINDING, WHICH IS THAT THESE RULES DID NOT FORM A SYSTEM: the 1582 compilation 'impuso tanto un blindaje debil como fuerte para las companias; de manera que el segundo hacia innecesario el primero. No obstante, esta incoherencia no fue detectada por los compiladores de la ley' (264). The cells should not be read as describing a regime.
PHASE SPLIT 2026-09-05 AT THE MAINTAINER'S INSTRUCTION, ON THE voc PRECEDENT OF 2026-08-29, AND THE COST IS STATED RATHER THAN DISGUISED. compagnie_antwerpen_1582 and compagnie_antwerpen_1608 SEPARATE ON EXACTLY TWO CELLS OF THIRTY-TWO - AP2 and FP4 - and on nothing else. Every other cell is identical in value, and most of the shared evidence sits in De ruysscher's section II.3, headed 'Persistencia del caracter personal de la sociedad (1582-1608)', which spans both phases by its own title. PROHIBITION, ON THE fraterna/compagnia MODEL OF 2026-08-31: these two rows are ONE SOURCE READ ONCE. They are not two independent cases, no agreement between them is a finding, and no similarity or difference claim on any component may count them as two. A third separating cell would appear at FP3 if the maintainer fixed that characteristic's definition - the 1608 phase legalised secret societies and the participatio while the 1582 phase did not - and FP3 is deliberately left .NR on both rows so that the separation is not manufactured by a definitional choice made after the split was ordered.
THE PHASE BOUNDARY IS TEXTUAL, NOT PRACTICAL, AND A READER MUST NOT TAKE IT FOR A CHANGE OF REGIME. De ruysscher records that the 1608 Compilatae 'no tuvo mucha influencia y el de 1582 siguio siendo el mas importante en la ciudad', that its burdensome commercial formalities 'no se acogieron favorablemente', that it was never printed, and that its 3,643 articles made copying so laborious that circulation was obstructed (255). Against that, the Antwerp government did order the city court to apply the 1608 chapters on mercantile agreements (255). So the 1608 row describes an enacted text of contested reach, not a regime that displaced its predecessor, and FP4=P on that row records exactly this.
THIS ROW IS THE COSTUYMEN IMPRESSAE OF 1582. It separates from compagnie_antwerpen_1608 on AP2=P against 0: the Impressae took Paolo di Castro's strong-shielding rule, so that company assets could not be seized or expropriated for a partner's personal debts (cap. 52 art. 5) and personal creditors claimed only after dissolution and out of the remainder (art. 6) (252), while a member could still force partition by an untimely renunciation (253) - hence P. And on FP4=0 against P: the Impressae impose no registration or publicity requirement on the partnership contract.
OUT OF SCOPE AND CODED FROM NOWHERE IN EITHER ANTWERP ROW: the reederij or ship co-ownership, whose co-owners were liable pro parte (Compilatae part 4 cap. 8 arts. 21-22, at 244 n 26) and which is already in this census as partenrederij; the commenda-type contract, of which De ruysscher says Antwerp instances were 'muy excepcionales' (250); the Antwerp natie, already a row and a different institution; and the whole of the HOLLAND AND VOC material at 257 and 261-263, per the maintainer's instruction of 2026-09-05 and because the census carries voc_1602, voc_1612 and voc_1623 coded from other sources. THE PARTICIPATIO IS NOT OUT OF SCOPE AS A POSITION - a particeps was a socius (258) - BUT IT MAY BE A THIRD FORM AND THAT QUESTION IS FLAGGED, NOT TAKEN. From 1608 the Compilatae excepted from in solidum liability those financial participants who did not appear in the firm's name and were not defined as 'socios' in the contract (260), and by then three kinds of non-active investor were distinguished, 'Todos tenian responsabilidad limitada' (256). A row scoping the Antwerp participatio would carry LR1=limited where these rows carry unlimited-joint; on the standing rule that a type spanning both values of a characteristic must be split, that is an argument for a separate row rather than for widening these.
HIS DISAGREEMENT WITH HANSMANN, KRAAKMAN AND SQUIRE IS CODED AS A DISAGREEMENT AND NOT RESOLVED, per the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-09-05. De ruysscher argues in terms against the HKS account: there was no preference for strong over weak entity shielding, economic growth did not depend on strong shielding, shielding was 'una cuestion nacida de las practicas de liquidacion y, ademas de ellas, de influencias culturales' rather than of legislative deliberation, and iura in rem were 'de caracter excepcional y de relevancia minima' (235-236, 238-239, 263-265). Antwerp at its height 'no contaba con un blindaje fuerte de las sociedades' and grew anyway (265). THE SPLIT MAKES THAT ARGUMENT VISIBLE IN THE MATRIX RATHER THAN BURYING IT IN A NOTE: AP2 goes from P to 0 across the phases while AP1 stays 1, which is his 'regresion a posiciones anteriores' (264) recorded as a coding.
